chapter: First bands and the road in the South
title: Coming home, his brother hoboing, and the suit in East St. Louis
summary: After a summer the brothers were sent money for the trip home; his brother hoboed, and Cootie bought his first long pants in East St. Louis.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: Yeah. Not coming out into the.-- so he was always himself, right then and there. Yeah. Yeah. I see. How long did you stay? Was it during one summer?

Yeah. It was during one summer. We got ready to come home, and our father sent us some money so we could come home, me and my brother. So my father sent us this money to come home, and my brother bought me a ticket and put me on the train, and he hoboed.
Was that what he wanted to do?
No, my father wasn't mad, because he knew him. He was --
That was quite nervy of him, wasn't it? What, was he only 15?
No, he was older than that.
But he was wild, you know.
Yeah. So he put you on a train.
Yeah. He put me on the train and he hoboed.
Where were you? Do you know?
Did you go -- during that summer, did you go to big towns?
Did you go to New Orleans?
The only place I can remember, a big town, was East St. Louis.
Because I bought me a suit there.

And the day I bought the suit, I worked in the carnival. They would be tearing it down. I would go and help them tear down the ferris wheel. I saved up that money. So when we got to East St. Louis, I went to a pawn shop and bought me a long pants suit.
I got me this suit. Yeah.
That was your first long pants?
No kidding. And then you started to wear it, right?
